texts: theres been a lot of noise outrage and badfaith framing around recent floorcrossings in parliament including the petition demanding mp michael ma resign and trigger a byelection but when you actually look at the numbers the law and parliamentary precedent the story starts to fall apart first the basics there is no legal requirement for an mp who crosses the floor to resign or run again thats not a loophole its how canadas parliamentary system has always worked mps are elected as individuals governments are formed based on who can command the confidence of the house the petition itself raised serious questions over 37000 signatures in four days from a riding where only about 53000 people voted in total in an election with a narrow twoparty split simply doesnt align with voter turnout or demographics even under the most generous assumptions the math doesnt convincingly add up cbcstyle analysis matters here because it asks the uncomfortable questions instead of amplifying outrage uncritically and then theres the broader claim being pushed by pierre poilievre that mark carney is somehow manipulating his way to a majority cbcs aaron wherry lays out why that framing collapses under scrutiny canadians dont vote for majority or minority governments they vote for mps those mps then decide who governs floorcrossing is not new conservatives have benefited from it liberals have benefited from it stephen harper explicitly defended mps right to cross the floor poilievre himself voted against legislation that would have forced floorcrossers into byelections confidenceandsupply agreements have delivered functional majorities without new elections none of this is unprecedented its parliamentary democracy this is exactly why the cbc matters not to tell canadians what to think but to explain how our democracy actually works to test claims against facts to provide context instead of slogans and to give people the tools to decide for themselves

i failed the bar exam again to illustrate my predicament ill need to briefly summarise the way legal education works in germany which is different from the american system that you might be familiar with basically after you finish the gymnasium the highest tier school you can go to law school its theoretically 45 years until you get your degree but almost everyone exceeds that timeframe sometimes greatly theres no compulsion to take the notoriously difficult graduation exam on schedule you can study as long as you want provided you can keep yourself afloat which i did by working as a courier for a pharmacy and receiving generous support from my family after taking all the classes people often spend an entire additional year or more taking preparatory classes with private tutors i passed the exams with a passing grade which took me almost a decade ill not dwell on the details of how that happened and why i didnt just drop out luckily i could boost my grade by doing well in elective classes that also factor into the final score also i dont have any debts because tuition fees are a fraction of what youd pay in the us or uk the thing is that a law degree is not very useful without also doing a second set of exams after the referendariat that is not a thing in the englishspeaking world but for practical purposes you can think of it as a postgraduate degree its really not because the university has got nothing to do with it classes and exams are held at the courthouse anyway you have new classes focused on litigation and trial law and do practical work at the court the prosecutors office and law firms of your choosing after just under two years you write a new set of exams all the while the government pays you a modest stipend i very narrowly failed the exams if that happens that is you fail you get sent to an additional course for four months focused on doing mock exams i did reasonably well there i always had a broadly correct idea of how to solve the mock exams and though id make mistakes id learn something from the classes where we discussed the exams and the solution so i was confident when going in to write my second attempt i wrote my second attempt in november and ill not be getting my results until the start of february but i already know i failed i know that sometimes people end up getting decent grades in exams they thought they bunked but this isnt one of those times it was brutal in all likelihood i did worse than in my first attempt i perceived the tasks to be significantly more difficult than all the mock exams i believe i passed four out of eight written exercises its theoretically possible to do that and still get a passing grade but its not going to be enough in my case in two cases i made unforgivably stupid mistakes that almost certainly ruined these exercises the good news is that because i but narrowly failed the first time ill get a third attempt the bad news is ill lose my stipend and have to request unemployment benefits while singing up for and writing my third and final attempt i already started cracking the books for that but it seems i already forgot half the required information its like my brain just cant absorb it pulling this off will require nerves of steel that frankly i dont have if i do pass its going to be rather awkward explaining to prospective employers why it took so long for me to graduate but if i fail my employment prospects are positively dire there are positions that you can fill with only the first degree but while the rates of failing your final attempt for the first exam are fairly high the ones for failing the second exam are low usually below 1 people who just dont cut it are usually weeded out beforehand but i somehow wasnt anyone ill send my cv to is going to quite reasonably assume that im stupid and incompetent and send it straight to the trash folder there are many people graduating law school with better grades to fill these openings i could maybe be a research assistant at a law firm but it doesnt pay well its usually a stopgap thing people do before they do the referendariat i would struggle to afford a bedsit much less nice things i could conceivably switch professions altogether but i straight up cant think of anything id be good at or where an employer wouldnt have significant reservations about hiring me very often ill be thinking that i should have trained as a paralegal or for a junior position in the civil service i might now have a steady decently paid job seeing as going back in time is not possible my thoughts keep turning to the other way out long term i dont see any other option because ill never be able to retire i only ever had a modest income and i so paid very little into the compulsory retirement insurace and what ill get out of it will translate to abject poverty and i dont know if the intervening decades will be worth it subsisting on benefits or struggling to make ends meet in menial jobs an election is a formal group decisionmaking process whereby a portion or all of a population or group votes to chooses an individual or multiple individuals to hold public office or other position of responsibility elections have been the usual mechanism by which modern representative democracy has operated since the 17th century elections may fill offices in the legislature sometimes in the executive and judiciary and for regional and local government such as cities or towns this process is also used in many other standardized associations public businesses and organizations from clubs to voluntary association and corporations the global use of elections as a tool for selecting representatives in modern representative democracies is in contrast with the practice in the democratic archetype ancient athens where the elections were considered an oligarchic institution and most political offices were filled using allotment which is also known as sortition by which office holders were chosen by lot electoral reform describes the process of introducing fair electoral systems where they are not in place or improving the fairness or effectiveness of existing systems psephology is the study of results and other statistics relating to elections especially with a view to predicting future results the term elect means to select or to nominate so sometimes other forms of balloting such as referendums are referred to as elections especially in the united states history elections were used as early in history as ancient greece and ancient rome and throughout the medieval period to select rulers such as the holy roman emperor see imperial election and the pope see papal election the pala king gopala ruled c 750s 770s ce in early medieval bengal was elected by a group of
